transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-01-28 15:30 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Maya, Ravi, Olivia (Redwood); Sara, Tom, Priya, Ethan (Lucent Labs)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — audio ok?
[00:07] Sara: Yep, good here.
[00:10] Maya: Awesome. Goal today: lock down renewal numbers, confirm EU+APAC activation windows, and scope the on-prem pilot for data residency. Ravi's gonna walk through the perf notes then we'll go security.
[00:25] Ravi: Cool. I'll start with a high level — last quarter your TTI spikes were at end-of-month due to batch backpressure, we suggested moving to a smaller steady reserve with burst capacity. We ran sample traces — the KV cash, sorry KV cache warming looked fine but you do get cold-start tail latencies.
[00:45] Tom: When you say cold-start tail, what's the 95th number?
[00:48] Ravi: On hosted with our default quantized runner we saw p95 ~ 220ms for short prompts, p99 drifted to 1.8s under first-byte for big seqs. With a lightweight pre-warm and prefix caching that drops dramatically — p95 ~ 80ms. These numbers depend on model size and whether you use dedicated pools.
[01:10] Sara: Those are promising. Our threshold for production is p95 under 150ms for chat surface, otherwise product team won't sign off.
[01:17] Ravi: Right — for that you want dedicated capacity or a reserved Dedicated-like pool. You can get consistent p95 < 120ms with Dedicated + warm box, and cheaper token costs per unit with batching. But there's the cost/latency tradeoff.
[01:30] Maya: And on pricing, we're proposing the renewal at the tier we talked about — 30% uplift in committed units vs. current, with burst credits and a 4-week step-up window. I'll send the updated worksheet after this call.
[01:43] Ethan: Quick question — we might need EU data residency for a subset of traffic. Can we route EU customers to EU-only geocluster in the first 60 days after renewal?
[01:51] Olivia: Yes — activation is largely config-driven on our side. The earliest realistic window for EU is ~6 weeks to provision and validate; APAC is usually 8-10 weeks depending on capacity availability. If you want faster we can do a private pilot in your cloud account.
[02:08] Priya: Regarding private pilot and on-prem — our compliance folks will need KMS/HSM integration details, proof of key separation, audit log retention, plus SOC2 evidence.
[02:17] Maya: Totally. We have a SOC2 pack and an HSM integration spec — I'll attach both. We also support bring-your-own-KMS via our private deployment.
[02:26] Priya: For BYOK we need a diagram of key flow and where tokenization happens.
[02:30] Ravi: We'll provide a flow diagram. Important nuance — in Private mode the control plane is customer-managed, the inference plane still needs certain network egress for updates unless fully air-gapped. We should clarify the "air-gapped" expectation.
[02:45] Tom: On the network side, what's the required ACL footprint for private? We need exact CIDR and port lists.
[02:49] Ravi: We'll share the ACL matrix; typically three egress endpoints: control plane, metrics/observability, and possible dedupe object store if you enable caching.
[02:58] Sara: Back to capacity: is there a way to auto-fallback to a cheaper model variant if Dedicated pool is saturated? We don't want end-users broken during peak.
[03:05] Ravi: Yes, smart routing supports policy-based fallback to model variants — you can set a route where latency priority prefers dedicated, cost-priority prefers hosted, with automatic fallback. There is also canary rollouts for model versions.
[03:18] Maya: That's in the console — you'll see routing policies and per-route dashboards. We'll include screenshots.
[03:25] Ethan: Are token cost buckets different for hosted vs dedicated? How do we forecast billing?
[03:29] Maya: Billing differs — hosted is usage-based per-token, dedicated includes committed units with overage rates. We'll give a forecast spreadsheet that maps expected token consumption per route and shows cost delta per scenario.
[03:40] Ravi: Also, Optimize suggestions can recommend quantization profiles to reduce cost without materially impacting output quality — we've got sample evaluations from similar workloads.
[03:50] Tom: How do those suggestions affect latency? Quantization sometimes adds decode CPU overhead.
[03:54] Ravi: It depends. For GPU-optimized quantized kernels we see minimal latency regression; sometimes throughput improves. I'll attach a table comparing int8/4/3-bit profiles across your median seq lengths.
[04:07] Maya: For the renewal term, any preferences on length? We can do 12 or 24 months. Longer term gives better committed pricing and faster provisioning guarantees.
[04:14] Sara: We prefer a 12-month with option to extend at predetermined step-ups. Team needs flexibility for next year's budget cycle.
[04:20] Maya: Sounds good. We'll propose a 12-month commit with a 3-step capacity ramp and reserved burst bucket.
[04:27] Priya: On compliance, timeline — we need the SOC2 addendum and KMS spec by next week to start legal review.
[04:33] Olivia: We'll prioritize that; I'll drop the docs in the shared folder today.
[04:37] Maya: Great. Pilot question — for on-prem pilot what does the handoff look like? Typically: week 0 preflight, week 1 infra provision, week 2 smoke and perf, week 3 scale tests, week 4 production cutover. Does that fit your cadence?
[04:51] Tom: Yes, though we might need two extra days for internal change windows.
[04:54] Ravi: Noted. For the perf plan we'll run a 24-hour cold start stress and a 4-hour sustained throughput run. We'll capture traces and KV-cache heatmap.
[05:06] Sara: Can you include example traces where we can see batch size distribution? That helps our SREs tune autoscaler.
[05:10] Ravi: Yep. We'll include batch histograms and the autoscaler policy suggestion.
[05:15] Ethan: Any blockers from your side for signing the renewal?
[05:18] Priya: Security needs the KMS spec plus confirmation on audit log retention (we require 13 months minimum). Also need SSO/SAML integration details and RBAC controls.
[05:27] Maya: We'll include SSO guides, RBAC matrix, and confirm audit retention is configurable to 13 months for private deployments.
[05:34] Olivia: I'll also include the on-call escalation matrix for the pilot.
[05:38] Maya: Great. Wrap-up recap: Maya to send updated pricing and committed units table; Ravi to run the perf tests and send traces; Olivia to attach SOC2 and KMS docs; Priya to circulate compliance question list. We'll aim to have signoff by 2025-02-10 and start pilot week of 2025-02-17.
[05:55] Tom: Sounds good. Thanks.
[05:58] Sara: Thanks everyone.
[06:00] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up with the folder link and timeline.

Notes about transcription: some technical terms were auto-transcribed imperfectly ("KV cash" instead of KV cache, "V P C" for VPC, "dedicated pool" sometimes labelled "dedicate pool"), speaker attribution occasionally merged in the middle of long answers.

References/Links shared during call: capacity_worksheet_v3.xlsx (Maya), perf-traces-20250127.zip (Ravi), SOC2-addendum.pdf (Olivia)

End of transcript.
